headline: Why is My Kitchen Still Sooty After I Cleaned It?
articleBody: It's super frustrating when you've put in the effort to clean up after a kitchen fire, only to find that pesky soot and smoke smell still hanging around. What gives? Well, soot isn't just surface-level dust; it's often oily and acidic, needing specialized techniques to remove completely. Many common household cleaners can actually smear the soot or drive it deeper into porous surfaces, making the problem worse. Plus, smoke particles can penetrate fabrics, drywall, and even into your HVAC system, leaving behind a persistent odor that regular cleaning won't touch. You might be missing hidden areas too, like inside cabinets, under appliances, or even in ceiling voids, where smoke and soot travel. Improper ventilation during cleanup can also re-deposit airborne particles. That's why professional fire damage restoration is so effective. We use industrial-grade equipment and cleaning solutions designed to neutralize odors and safely remove soot from all types of surfaces, preventing secondary damage and ensuring your kitchen truly feels clean again.
